macro.headline: Risk-on tape, broad participation, but momentum indicators lag price
macro.story:
The tape is constructive. SPY sits above both its 50- and 200-day moving averages, +8.4% above the 200-day, with the Engine C state machine reading CALM and no washout active. VIX has collapsed roughly 15% over five days to 16.1, and the VIX3M/VIX ratio is in healthy contango — fear has drained out of the system. Eight of eleven GICS sectors are above their 50-day moving averages, S&P 500 component breadth runs 65% bullish versus 16% bearish, and small-caps (Russell 2000 RSI 59.6) are participating alongside the Dow — this is broad, not narrow, leadership.

The dominant cross-asset catalyst grounded in the active theme data is the Geopolitical Risk Unwind around the Iran/Hormuz situation: WTI crude has crashed 27% over 21 days into oversold territory (RSI 30.5), VIX has unwound, and the AI Infrastructure Build-Out theme (CHASING stage) is absorbing capital rotating out of defensive hedges — gold is down 4.3% over 21 days with DXY firm, the textbook inverse relationship at work. Lower oil takes pressure off CPI prints and supports the rate-sensitive corners of the market; that, in turn, helps explain why Financials, Healthcare, Materials, Real Estate and Industrials are all HOT simultaneously while Energy and Communication Services are weak.

The tension worth respecting: SPY's MACD histogram is still negative (-3.63) and below its signal line despite price strength — momentum is lagging price, which often shows up at the late-stage of a leg before a pause or shallow pullback. QQQ jumped 3.1% intraday on the most recent print but its MACD is also bearish. The yield curve has flattened sharply (10Y-2Y spread down 21% over 21 days), which is not an immediate sell signal but is a quiet warning that bond markets are pricing in slower growth ahead. Confidence is capped at MEDIUM because of the price/momentum divergence even though every other indicator points the same way.

For a long-only book, the playbook is straightforward: hunt longs in the HOT sectors via the Early-Runway industries flagged below, respect that some leaders are extended (RSIs >70), and use the validated Accumulation Screen geometry to time entries rather than chasing breakouts blindly.

active.name: Geopolitical Risk Unwind — Iran Deal / Hormuz Reopening
active.thesis: The Iran nuclear deal and the Strait of Hormuz reopening have resolved near-term crude supply-disruption risk. WTI crude has fallen approximately 5% to near $80/barrel as the geopolitical risk premium unwinds. This is unambiguously RISK-ON for equities: lower crude reduces input-cost and inflation-expectation pressure, eases the case for further Fed tightening, and removes the dominant macro tail-risk from the narrative. The correct read on oil weakness here is NOT 'Iran re-escalation risk' — it is the OPPOSITE: the Hormuz corridor is reopening and supply constraints are lifting. Energy equities (XLE, E&P names) face near-term margin compression from lower realized prices, but the broader equity market benefits. Transports and consumer discretionary are direct fuel-cost beneficiaries.
